summary: Tested the new P2P Live Trade feature end-to-end with two users (A=Demo Survivor, B=Demo Trader). Backend: 5/6 tests passing; presence via WS, invite/accept/reject, offer, lock, confirm+atomic swap, cancel, security (untradeable dinosaurs, over-qty, amber daily cap, both-locked-required) all validated. Frontend: full flow verified in two browser contexts — presence, invite popup, waiting popup, accept -> both enter room, live offer sync (item + amber), lock, confirm, return to lobby, cooldown tag. Sound clicks fire. One critical backend bug discovered: on swap the delivered item is inserted with item_id=null because /trade/offer stores the offer snapshot WITHOUT the item_id field, so _execute's _add_item receives snap.item_id=None and creates broken inventory rows.

critical.issue: The offer snapshot persisted in trade_sessions omits item_id (only inv_id/qty/name/image/category/rarity/tier are stored). When _execute delivers items to the other side, _add_item(other, snap, qty) inserts a new inventory row with item_id=None. Confirmed live: after successful trade, A's inventory contains a 'Huevo Raro' row with item_id=None. This breaks future item matching (stacking, market filters, image swaps, cooldown/skins logic keyed by item_id). Fix: include 'item_id': s['item_id'] in the dict written to {side}_offer.items inside live_trade.py set_offer().

minor.issue: When a user toggles lock from locked->unlocked, only their own side unlocks (the other side stays locked). This is technically correct per code but the button label on the still-locked partner remains 'Desbloquear', so partner must manually unlock to edit. Consider clarifying via UI hint (spec explicitly requires reset-both only on OFFER edits, so this is by design; document only).
There is no server-side validation that prevents an item snapshot from being displayed if item_id is missing (see critical above).

integration_issues.issue: React console warning: 'Encountered two children with the same key' (AnimatedSlots). Non-blocking but indicates a key collision when the offer list transiently contains duplicate inv_id entries during re-renders after lock reset.

action_items: FIX (CRITICAL): In /app/backend/live_trade.py inside set_offer(), add 'item_id': s['item_id'] to the per-item dict written under {side}_offer.items so the swap can carry it into the receiver's inventory row. Without this, all traded items land in the receiver with item_id=null.
Investigate the duplicate React key warning in AnimatedSlots (TradeRoom.jsx). Likely add a fallback key like `${it.inv_id}-${it.qty}` or dedupe items by inv_id before render.
critical_code_review_comments: live_trade.py set_offer(): missing item_id in the stored offer snapshot (source of the null item_id bug on delivery).

live_trade.py _add_item(): safe against duplicate stacking, but relies on item_id which is None from the swap — will always create a brand-new stack instead of merging. Once item_id is preserved, revalidate this path.
live_trade.py: OK — indexes are created, ObjectIds are stripped ({_id:0}) everywhere, atomic $inc/$gte guard on _dec_item is correct, rollback logic on failed decs is present.
live_trade.py cancel: does not push a 'trade_cancelled' event to the initiator's own tab, only the other side. Not a bug, just noting.
TradeRoom.jsx: uses inv_id as the React key on <motion.div> inside <AnimatedSlots>; when receiving a snapshot that briefly duplicates inv_id (edit-then-relock), React warns. Consider composite key.

Also reset user cooldowns between reruns: db.users.update_many({}, {$unset:{last_item_trade_at:'',trade_amber_day:'',trade_amber_sent:''}}). Presence/invite/room UI already validated end-to-end.
rca of the issue: In /app/backend/live_trade.py (function set_offer around L423-L427), the persisted offer item dict is: {inv_id, qty, name, image, category, rarity, tier} — missing item_id. Later, _execute() iterates these dicts and calls _add_item(other, it, qty), where _add_item builds the DB doc via snap.get('item_id') -> None. Reproduction: seed A/B, run test_full_trade_flow, inspect A's inventory post-swap: the received 'Huevo Raro' row has item_id=None. Mitigation: include 'item_id': s['item_id'] alongside the other fields when writing {side}_offer.items in set_offer().
